title: gRPC and Protocol Buffers
description: Discover how gRPC and Protocol Buffers enable high-performance, typed communication between services.

data.text: In modern backend systems, services often need to call each other across network boundaries. REST with JSON is popular, but it is verbose and loosely typed. gRPC (gRPC Remote Procedure Call) and Protocol Buffers offer an alternative: a fast, binary, strongly-typed contract between services.

gRPC was developed by Google and is now an open-source Cloud Native Computing Foundation project. It uses HTTP/2 under the hood, supports streaming in all directions, and generates client libraries in many languages from a single schema file.

Protocol Buffers, or protobuf, is a language-neutral, platform-neutral serialization format. You define your data structures in a .proto file, then run a compiler that generates code in your chosen language. The generated code handles serialization, deserialization, and type checking for you.

data.text: Why Protobuf Beats JSON for Internal APIs

data.title: Protobuf Advantages
items: Smaller payloads — binary encoding is 3 to 10 times smaller than JSON.
Faster serialization — no string parsing, no reflection overhead.
Strong typing — schema violations become compile-time errors, not runtime surprises.
Built-in documentation — the .proto file is the single source of truth for your API.

data.text: gRPC calls look like local function calls, but they travel over the network. The client sends a request message; the server returns a response message. Under the hood, gRPC uses HTTP/2, which gives it multiplexing, header compression, and persistent connections automatically.

data.title: gRPC Communication Patterns
items: Unary — one request, one response. The most common pattern.
Server streaming — one request, many responses. Useful for feeds or logs.
Client streaming — many requests, one response. Useful for uploading large files.
Bidirectional streaming — both sides send a stream of messages. Useful for chat or real-time coordination.

cards.title: REST with JSON
pros: Easy to test with curl or a browser

cards.title: gRPC with Protobuf
cons: Binary format is hard to inspect manually

data.title: When to Reach for gRPC
data.text: gRPC shines in internal service-to-service communication where latency and throughput matter. It is less suited for public APIs consumed by browsers unless you add a gRPC-Web proxy. For public APIs, REST or GraphQL often remain simpler choices.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Protocol Buffers define a compact, typed schema for data exchange.
gRPC uses HTTP/2 and protobuf to deliver high-performance RPC communication.
gRPC supports four streaming patterns, making it versatile for microservices.
Choose gRPC for internal APIs where performance and contracts matter; use REST for public, browser-facing APIs.
data.takeaway: gRPC is not just a transport protocol — it is an entire ecosystem for building strongly-typed, high-performance distributed systems.
